MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 18, 2023

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:03 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chambers,
  4045 Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR BAIN.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR BAIN led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope,  Ciarolla,  Johnson,  Holdsworth
  McCormick, and Bain

  Commissioners Absent:  Persichina

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION LEFT COUNCIL CHAMBER TO
  CONDUCT A PARK TOUR OF THE PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER**

  4.  PARK TOURS

  A.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER (VERBAL REPORT)

  Peter Weber Equestrian Center (PWEC) Operator Gil Houle gave a brief overview
  of the programs, activities, and boarding practices at the PWEC.

  ACM Davis gave an update regarding the prefabricated restroom facility that will be
  installed at the PWEC.

  PWEC Operator Houle led the Commission on a walking tour of the facility showing
  the different boarding stalls and other amenities at the PWEC.

  Superintendent Goldsmith showed the Commission the site where the new
  restroom facility would be installed.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 18, 2023
   VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK asked if the land was still shifting inside the Landfill
  area and around the surrounding area. PWEC Operator Houle and Staff stated that
  the land is still shifting and sinking in certain areas.

  CHAIR BAIN asked about the coyote situation inside the Landfill and surrounding
  areas. Staff indicated that there have been some reports in the past regarding
  coyotes in this area, but it appears not to be as prevalent recently.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked about the camps offered after. PWEC
  Operator Houle stated that on Tuesday-Thursday they offer a one-day camp from
  3:30-5:30pm. He stated that the age range is 3-12 years old, and the younger kids
  start with pony rides and the older kids will do a horse ride along a trail.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION LEFT THE PWEC AND RETURNED BACK
  TO COUNCIL CHAMBERS TO CONTINUE THE MEETING**

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF JULY 17,
  2023

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  HOLDSWORTH to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  July 17, 2023.

  There being no objection, CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  FOUNDERS PARK PROJECT ALTERNATIVES

  ACM Davis provided a brief overview of the Founders Park project and the
  alternative approaches to the project as reviewed at the August 8 City Council
  meeting (as per the agenda material).

  ACM Davis stated that due to the City being a smaller city, it has been difficult to
  get competitive bids for small projects.. She also noted that as a government entity
  the City must follow a bid process which incorporates prevailing wage, which is an
  added expense. She stated that Staff has had difficulty understanding how the

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 18, 2023
   second bid came in higher when the scope of the work went down from the first bid
  process, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  ACM Davis noted that the contractor did line item their bid for both bids and noted
  that they bumped up some costs and lowered others between the first and second
  bids, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH noted that the staff report does include the
  contractors’ estimate for certain line items included in the project. ACM Davis stated
  that the estimate included is only for the second bid process and that the first bid
  was not included in report packet. She further explained that the City’s Public
  Works Director did complete a breakdown and compared the two bids. She also
  noted that as a public entity the City does not have the ability to negotiate with the
  contractor since their first bid was lower than the second bid and can only go with
  the lowest responsive bidder or reject the bid and reevaluate the project.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if the $150,000 that is allocated will cover the first
  phase that is proposed. ACM Davis stated that there is a good chance that the bid
  will come in over that amount, but that that Staff feels comfortable that the number
  is more accurate for just the landscaping of the project and that City maintenance
  staff could also complete some of the aspects of the project. She also noted that
  the amount is comparable to the City Hall landscape project and that the City will
  not need the level of professional overhead with a landscape contract.

  ACM Davis stated that the $150,000 for this project has been allocated and
  approved with the current budget and that the money can be allocated for
  Phase Two in the following year, if necessary, in response to COMMISSIONER
  POPE.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that she has seen this project take a long time and
  would like to see the project get started and moved that the Commission accept
  Staff’s recommendation to consider completing the project in two phases.

  CHAIR BAIN stated that she had a concern over completing the project in phases
  because typically when you divide things up it becomes more expensive in the
  second phase than originally anticipated.

  CHAIR BAIN also asked if someone went through the bids to analyze the
  correctness of the quotes on the line items in the bid as she saw some interesting
  numbers in the attached bid. ACM Davis stated that the City’s Public Works Director
  and the City’s engineering contractor, Wildan, analyze the data with the bids and
  have more of the expertise in understanding the different costs of these type of line
  items associated with this kind of project.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 18, 2023
   ACM Davis stated that the City’s Public Works Director and Wildan Engineering
  recommended rejecting the $544,870 bid from KASA Construction. This
  recommendation was established based on reducing some costs of the original
  scope of work after the first bid process and seeing the second bid come in even
  higher than the first bid. She also stated options include to complete project with
  with the larger Nature Center project or to break the project into two phases and
  focus the first bid on landscape contractors to assist in receiving a more respectable
  bid, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  CHAIR BAIN asked if a landscape contractor would be able to complete the plans
  as originally conceived. ACM Davis stated that Staff is confident that a landscape
  contractor can successfully complete the project with possibly some minor
  modifications.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK asked if the two-phase project option would be able to
  be completed in back-to-back fiscal years. ACM Davis affirmed that is the intent of
  the project completion. She also suggested if it was a priority to the Commission,
  they could include that request within their recommendation to the City Council.
  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK noted it would be nice to see a phased plan in place to
  see the project get started in the short term.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that there has been a delay in the Nature Center
  project as well and that she is concerned in bringing this project to be a part of the
  larger Nature Center project that it could cause another delay in accomplishing the
  Founders Park project.

  ACM Davis stated that Staff shared a Wildan Engineering estimate with the
  contractors during the bid process to help the contractors know what a feasible
  amount for the project is. She also stated that it was difficult for Staff to see the
  increase in the amounts of the bids for this project in the second round of bids, in
  response to CHAIR BAIN.

  CHAIR BAIN asked if landscape contractors were invited to participate in the bid
  process. ACM Davis stated that it is an open bid process, but typically a landscape
  contractor will not participate in the scope of work attached to this bid process based
  on the playground equipment portion of the contract.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked if we do the project in different phases and
  spend the allocated budgeted amount on the landscaping phase would there be
  additional costs associated with the upkeep of the area prior to the start of the
  second phase of the project that could be a budget concern. ACM Davis stated that
  she did not see this as being a budget concern for maintenance purposes prior to
  the second phase being completed. She also stated that it would allow the space

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 18, 2023
   to be a usable space in the meantime before playground equipment is installed
  which would justify the new maintenance costs associated with a new park space.

  ACM Davis stated that the City Council has rejected the KASA Construction bids
  and the City would not be moving forward with them regarding this project under
  the current scopey. She also stated that City Council requested that the alternatives
  listed in the report be presented to the Commission to then make a recommendation
  to the City Council on the best way to proceed. She noted that Staff recommends
  going with the two-phase alternative as it appears to be more feasible based on the
  budget. ACM Davis also suggested that there is an opportunity for the Commission
  to decide the overall importance of still including the play equipment as a part of
  the project, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that the opportunity in doing the project in phases
  is that the Commission could reassess this in a year and still try to keep the original
  integrity of the project. She noted that this would allow the Commission to see if
  what is accomplished with the first phase is what the public may want with this park
  space even possibly without the play equipment.

  CHAIR BAIN suggested that the bid be put out for two phases but at the same time.
  COMMISSION POPE noted that most landscape contractors would not be able to
  complete the play equipment scope of work of the second phase. COMMISSIONER
  HOLDSWORTH noted that there would more likely be higher bids with the second
  phase of the project based on the ambiguity of what might need to be redone with
  the first phase to accomplish the scope of work of the second phase. ACM Davis
  stated that the City is limited because of already having gone out to bid for a full
  project and due to Public Works requirements.

  ACM Davis stated that the rock feature associated with the original plans is
  considered a climbing feature which would be considered play equipment, in
  response to VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  ACM Davis stated that Staff does feel that City Council would be open to approving
  a two-phase option and that the idea is that each phase would cost around
  $150,000, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  COMMISSIONER POPE moved to accept Staff’s recommendation to present the
  project in phase one with landscaping and construction in this current fiscal year
  and phase two to include the installation of play equipment in the next fiscal year to
  COUNCIL. VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK issued a second to the motion presented
  by COMMISSIONER POPE.

  CHAIR BAIN asked to understand better what type of contractor would be retained
  to rebid the project in two phases. ACM Davis stated that Staff would follow its

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 18, 2023
   normal bid process for a Public Works contract and would anticipate landscape
  contractors being the majority of the bids for the first phase of the project with other
  construction firms completing bids for the second phase of the project when that
  contract becomes available.

  CHAIR BAIN requested that the original motion be amended to have Staff look at
  the scope of work in phase one to consider any additional cost savings.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH requested that the motion be amended to
  consider that the bid proposal for phase one avoid any inefficiencies or work that
  would need to be redone in phase two, so plants or materials that were installed in
  phase one would not need to be removed during the second phase of the project.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK,
  amended by CHAIR BAIN and COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH TO APPROVE
  AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  TO RECOMMEND TO CITY COUNCIL STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION TO
  COMPLETE THE PROJECT WITH A PHASE ONE AND PHASE TWO IN
  CONSECUTIVE FISCAL YEARS BUT IN ADDITION ASK THAT STAFF
  LOOK AT THE SCOPE OF WORK FOR ANY ADDITIONAL COST
  SAVINGS THAT MAY BE RECOGNIZED AND ALSO TO AVOID
  INEFFICIENCIES AND ANY POTENTIAL REWORK DONE TO PHASE
  TWO TO NOT UNDO ANYTHING IN PHASE ONE.

  AYES:  Pope, Ciarolla, Johnson, Holdsworth, McCormick and Bain
  ABSENT:  Persichina

  B.  2023 HILLS ARE ALIVE DEBRIEF

  Coordinator Morrow provided a brief overview of the debrief of the 2023 Hills Are
  Alive 5k/10k Race (as per the agenda material).

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked how the resulting net revenue of this year’s event
  compared to the net revenue of previous years. Coordinator Morrow stated that the
  previous years’ net revenue was more than this year’s net revenue.
  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if Staff felt this difference was due to the added
  expenses of the chip timer and DJ to the 2023 race. Coordinator Morrow concurred
  that Staff did feel that those added expenses were one of the main reasons this
  year’s race did have a little less net revenue.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if Staff could remove the last bullet point in the
  considerations for next year section of the debrief as she believes runners are not
  interested in having Red Bull or Monster energy drinks. Staff agreed with this

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
SEPTEMBER 18, 2023
   assessment and noted that they will remove the item prior to submitting the debrief
  at the next Council meeting.

  CHAIR BAIN asked whether any expenses could be decreased and if the increase
  in the registration would assist with the added costs. Coordinator Morrow stated
  that the idea to increase the current registration fees by $5 was to assist in covering
  the added expenses to bring the net revenue closer to the previous years in future
  years.

  CHAIR BAIN asked whether the sponsorship revenue has stayed consistent.
  Coordinator Morrow stated that the sponsorship revenue has stayed consistent with
  previous years and that many of the current sponsors continue to return each year.

  CHAIR BAIN asked if the charge to the runners covers the expense of the medals
  and t-shirts. She noted that this would allow the entry fees to cover the overall
  expenses of the race and allow the sponsorship revenue to be donated to the
  Pepper Tree Foundation. Coordinator Morrow stated that this would be a good
  model to look into for previous years and is one of the reasons why Staff has looked
  into raising the entry fees.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA stated that people liked the chip timing aspect of the
  race this year. She stated that serious runners do enjoy using this race as an
  opportunity to time themselves. She noted that there is an opportunity to find a
  balance between the race being for serious runners and a community fun run event.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that she agreed with COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA
  that the race should include the serious runners and members from the community
  and that the updated price point still services both parties.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the extra additional items brought in for this
  year’s race shows the community that the City has raised the level of this event and
  made it more enjoyable allowing the event to attract more runners next year.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that the entry fee could be raised again in a few
  years as entry fees are going up with other races around the area.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH stated that runners look forward to certain races
  each year and having these extra perks will get them excited to participate in this
  race each year. COMMISSIONER POPE stated that once a runner participates in
  a race year after year, they really are not looking at the entry fee price.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA stated that her husband has been a sponsor for the
  race for the past years and has enjoyed walking in this race, but that she feels that
  there has been a push to attract runners more than walkers in the past couple of

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
SEPTEMBER 18, 2023
   years. She noted that she feels this may lessen the community aspect of the race
  if we discourage walkers from participating. COMMISSIONER POPE agreed that
  walkers should not be discouraged, and the race start times can be staggered to
  better accommodate both runners and walkers at the event. ACM Davis clarified
  that in 2022 there were some 10k walkers that presented a challenge to the timing
  of the event. She stated that there are many people on hand to manage the route
  of the race and that it is difficult to keep track of the 10k walkers throughout the
  route. She also stated that the event has a lot of 5k walkers and are absolutely
  encouraged to participate. COMMISSIONER JOHNSON stated that there may be
  a way to present a certain time period for the event to be able to still allow walkers.
  This would give them a time allotment that they would need to complete the race
  for the race sweepers to complete their job at the end of the race.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK stated that he has been at other events where
  organizations could sponsor and cover the costs of certain items like medals and t-
  shirts for the event where their business logo would only be on the t-shirt rather
  than all event sponsors being on the t-shirt. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that
  currently the sponsorships for City events are tiered at certain levels with certain
  benefits that increase based on the level of sponsorship, in response to CHAIR
  BAIN. ACM Davis stated that a sponsorship packet for all City events was
  introduced in 2019 and could be reviewed by the COMMISSION in January.

  COMMISSIONER POPE requested to add a bullet point to the considerations for
  next year section in the debrief to reexamine the sponsorship levels, types and
  benefits for the race.

  C.  RESCHEDULING OF CHANDLER PRESERVE TOUR (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas offered some options regarding the Chandler Preserve Park
  tour due to the cancellation of the August meeting. The first option was to forgo the
  park tour for this year. The second option was to complete the tour at the next
  meeting. The third option was to have a member of the land conservancy come to
  an upcoming meeting to present a report. The Commission agreed that option to
  have a member of the land conservancy come to an upcoming meeting to present
  a report would be best..

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  CONCERT IN THE PARK DEBRIEF (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the Concert in the Park event. He
  spoke about the overall event and mentioned that the band gave a wonderful
  performance and everyone in attendance appeared to have a great time.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
SEPTEMBER 18, 2023
   VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK asked if Staff showed pictures from previous years in
  the social media marketing of the event. ACM Davis stated that this concert event
  was a different style of event than previous years but pictures from this year’s event
  could be used in future marketing if the event is similar next year. Supervisor
  Pinuelas stated that Staff took many pictures at this year’s event and will look at
  using those pictures in the marketing for next year if the event is similar.

  ACM Davis stated that the Concert in the Park is a budgeted event, in response to
  COMMISSIONER POPE.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff would look into the LA County Performance
  Arts Grant for next year’s event, in response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  B.  CITY CELEBRATION UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow provided a brief overview of the upcoming City Celebration. He
  spoke about the location, event activities, the new BBQ lunch service option, and
  the schedule of events.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK asked if there was a way to market the events to the
  HOA’s in the City. ACM Davis noted that Staff does have a local HOA email list
  where the City emails HOA contacts requesting for them to share the information
  out to their members. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that there is also a bulk mailout
  of the flyer with the free activity passes attached to every residence. Some
  members of the Commission did state that they did not receive the mailout for this
  year. ACM Davis also noted that the event flyers are sent to the local schools for
  the principals to add to their digital flyer emails, in response to VICE CHAIR
  MCCORMICK.

  C.  TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLE TENNIS TOURNAMENT (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow provided a brief overview of the upcoming Tracy Austin Tennis
  Tournament. He spoke about the locations, registration, breakdown of the
  tournament, and the marketing of the event.

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided information regarding the sponsors of the event and
  stated that Staff is actively looking for additional sponsors, in response to CHAIR
  BAIN.

  D.  HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an overview of the upcoming Holiday Parade of
  Lights. She stated that Staff had been unable to make contact with the previous
  parade coordinator, Pageantry Parades. She stated that Staff had made the

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  9
SEPTEMBER 18, 2023
   decision to work with a new parade coordinator for this year’s event and hoped that
  everything was okay with the owner of Pageantry Parades. She stated that the new
  company Staff would hopefully be working with is named Soundskilz. She noted
  that Soundskilz is well versed in large City events including parades and that Staff
  will be presenting their contract to City Council at their next meeting and will report
  back to the Commission at a later time.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that it would be good to not present any additional
  events or activities for the remainder of this year as there will be additional work
  this year to organize the parade.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff anticipated the compensation for this new
  parade coordinator to be an additional $10,000 than paid in previous years and that
  City Council would assess the contract and associated budget, in response to
  CHAIR BAIN.

  E.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.
